title: Example 18-9: Diagramming with Underlining

illustrates.quote: Linear diagramming shows sentence structure, using font attributes to distinguish between parts of speech. Use transcriber-defined typeform indicators if needed (as seen for the double underlining in the example below). Use 1-3 margins for each diagrammed sentence.

blocks.text: In the following sentence the single underlined word is the verb and the double underlined words are a prepositional phrase.

Diagrammed sentence (back-translated): "We arrived at the hotel in the evening." with "arrived" single-underlined (the verb) and "at the hotel" double-underlined (the prepositional phrase), at a required 1-3 margin (18.7.1). Not modeled: F-188 (Emboss’s TYPEFORM has only one underline bit, so a second, visually distinct double-underline cannot be produced) and F-189 (no 1-3 "diagrammed sentence" margin exists; an ordinary paragraph defaults to a different indent).

print.printFeatures: single underline under 'arrived', double underline under 'at the hotel'

braille.notes: Re-extracted from source (lines 14629-14633, margin 9); matches both runs byte-for-byte.

resolution: Braille already agreed and re-extraction confirms it exactly; the diagrammed sentence and its single/double-underline distinction confirmed by back-translation. Kept the intro sentence as an ordinary, representable paragraph but the diagrammed sentence itself as 'other' (F-188 + F-189 both apply and neither is fixable by choosing different wording).
